23/S0.subgoal: Explain the motivation for treating XR systems as interactive systems and describe the disappearing-technology ideal, relating it to presence and historical computing trends.

23/S1.subgoal: Explain that interactive systems involve lay users and why designers should avoid forcing users to learn the underlying technology.

23/S2.subgoal: Describe the user-centric approach to designing interactive systems.

23/S3.subgoal: Define human-computer interaction and identify its core concern as incorporating humans into design.

23/S4.subgoal: Explain why human factors require knowing user characteristics, using a railway ticket-booking example to show that different users need different interfaces.

23/S5.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture and preview the next part.

goal.goal: Explain why XR systems are interactive systems guided by the disappearing-technology ideal and why HCI and human factors require designing them as user-centric systems for lay users with different characteristics.
goal.achieves: It provides the conceptual foundation for the course's human-factors and user-experience topics, helping the learner understand the user perspective that should inform designing and implementing an XR system.

objectives.goal: Frame XR as an interactive, disappearing technology oriented toward presence and explain why this means designers should accommodate lay users instead of requiring them to master the technology.
objectives.achieves: It gives the learner an interactive-systems baseline for interpreting XR's human-factors and user-experience focus in later lectures.

objectives.goal: Describe how human-computer interaction and human factors make interactive-system design user-centric by requiring interfaces to reflect user characteristics.
objectives.achieves: It lets the learner evaluate XR interface and system-design choices using the user-centered criteria emphasized in the course.
